name: Stringy Cosmic Strings
description: A straight string with finite energy per unit length, a curved transverse space, and a hidden torus whose shape changes with position around it.
convention: We use units with $c=1$. The coordinates describe regions away from the poles of the modular invariant.
history: A hidden torus changes shape from place to place around a straight string. After a circuit of the string, its shape returns with the two cycles of the torus relabelled, leaving the same physical torus [harveyroyston2008, greene1990stringy]. Brian R. Greene, Alfred Shapere, Cumrun Vafa, and Shing-Tung Yau introduced these stringy cosmic strings in 1990 [harveyroyston2008, greene1990stringy]. The torus is part of the compact space hidden at each point of the four dimensional spacetime [vafa1996ftheory].¶Write $z=x+iy$ for position across the string and $\tau=\tau_1+i\tau_2$ for the shape of the torus, with $\tau_2>0$. The four dimensional line element is $ds^2=-dt^2+dw^2+H(z,\bar z)\,dz\,d\bar z$, with $w$ along the string [harveyroyston2008]. For strings at the poles $z_i$ of $j(\tau(z))=P(z)/Q(z)$, $H=\tau_2|\eta(\tau)|^4\prod_i|z-z_i|^{-1/6}$, where $j$ is the modular invariant normalized by $j(i)=1$, $\eta$ is the Dedekind eta function, and $P$ and $Q$ are polynomials [harveyroyston2008]. The polynomials obey conditions at the values $j=0$ and $j=1$ that keep the shape holomorphic across those points [harveyroyston2008].¶The energy per unit length of an isolated straight string of a broken global $U(1)$ symmetry grows logarithmically with distance from its core [steinschabesburd1988]. For stringy cosmic strings, the relabelling identifies shapes related by $SL(2,\mathbb Z)$ and permits finite energy per unit length [vafa1996ftheory]. The same physical shape can therefore return after a circuit even when its label $\tau$ changes [vafa1996ftheory]. In some of these solutions the hidden space decompactifies near a core while the full higher dimensional geometry remains nonsingular [vafa1996ftheory, greene1990stringy].¶Gary W. Gibbons, Michael B. Green, and Malcolm J. Perry found a seven brane of type IIB supergravity with the same transverse geometry [gibbonsgreenperry1996]. For their single pole solution the space far from the brane approaches a cone with deficit angle $\pi/6$ [gibbonsgreenperry1996]. In the family with a finite limiting shape at infinity, $N$ poles contribute a total deficit $N\pi/6$; twelve poles give an asymptotic cylinder and twenty four close the transverse space into a sphere [harveyroyston2008]. The sphere has a total deficit of $4\pi$ [harveyroyston2008].¶In type IIB the field $\tau$ combines the axion and the dilaton and transforms like the shape of a torus [vafa1996ftheory]. Vafa used the geometry of a torus over the transverse sphere to construct a compact seven brane configuration in F-theory [vafa1996ftheory]. The sphere carries twenty four seven branes, and the torus over it forms a K3 surface [vafa1996ftheory].

related.text: The exterior of the Vilenkin-Gott string is a flat cone, and the stringy cosmic string has a curved transverse space that approaches a cone far away [gott1985, gibbonsgreenperry1996].
A point particle removes a wedge from a flat plane, and enough particles close space on itself [deser1984, gibbonsgreenperry1996].
A global monopole's scalar field spreads its energy away from its core, and the stringy cosmic string also carries a scalar field across its transverse space [barriola1989, vafa1996ftheory].
A compact direction changes over space around the Kaluza-Klein monopole, and a compact torus changes shape around the stringy cosmic string [sorkin1983, vafa1996ftheory].
